system.name: JANUS
system.one_liner: a cross-world, cooperative nested-virtualization hypervisor design that secures containers with efficient three-level address translation

components.name: L2
components.role: guest whose access to an unmapped GPA_L2 triggers the fault

components.name: v_ring0
components.role: L2's virtualized ring0 (kernel) execution context, containing the #PF handler

components.name: #PF Handler
components.role: L2's own page-fault handler, invoked once L0 has fixed the mapping

components.name: GPT_L1
components.role: page table for the L1 hypervisor's own address space

components.name: #VE Handler
components.role: L1's virtualization-exception handler, which receives the #VE raised when GPA_L2 lacks a mapping in EPT0→2

components.name: #HC Handler
components.role: L0's hypercall handler, which receives the JANUS_MAP mapping request from L1

components.name: EPT0→2
components.role: the single EPT that L0 fixes with the new GPA_L2-to-HPA mapping

flows.what: #VE exception (VM exit): GPA_L2 lacks a valid mapping in EPT0→2
L1 walks GPT_L1 and issues a KVM_HC_JANUS_OPS hypercall carrying GPA_L1 and GPA_L2
L0 locates the host physical address for GPA_L1 and fixes EPT0→2 for GPA_L2
resume L1 after the mapping is installed
resume L2 via VM entry now that the fault is resolved

content.key_idea: A GPA_L2 fault raises a lightweight #VE straight to L1, which resolves the mapping and asks L0 to fix EPT0→2 via one hypercall, costing only two exits instead of a full nested VM-exit chain.
content.reading_order: Top-down through three bands (L2, L1 ring0, L0 ring0), following circled steps 1-5 down from L2's fault through the #VE/#HC handlers to the EPT fix, then back up.

fill for the GPT_L1 and EPT0→2 table boxes

style.font: Times New Roman serif, 6.5pt, math symbols in Cambria Math
style.arrows: thin orthogonal arrows with filled heads and 5 circled step numbers
style.icons: bitmap: a handful of icons covering over half the figure area

encoding.color_means: peach marks the three fault/exception handlers (#PF, #VE, #HC) that do the fault-resolution work; blue marks guest execution contexts; gray marks the raw page-table/EPT data structures being read or fixed
encoding.emphasis: a circled 1-5 sequence forms a down-then-up loop through the three privilege bands, emphasizing that only two exits (to L1, then to L0) are needed to resolve the fault
reusable_patterns: numbered down-and-back-up exception path through stacked privilege layers
weaknesses: heavy use of bitmap icons for over half the figure area limits how much can be verified from vector text alone

evidence: when a GPAL2 lacks a valid mapping in EPT0→2 (Figure 9), a #VE is raised and delivered to L1
issues a KVM_HC_JANUS_OPS hypercall with JANUS_MAP operation
requires only a single lightweight exit to L1 followed by one exit to L0

summary: Figure 9 traces JANUS's EPT-fault handling path end to end. When L2 accesses a GPA_L2 with no mapping in EPT0→2, a hardware #VE (not a full VM exit) is delivered straight to L1's #VE Handler (step 1). The handler inspects the faulting address, walks its own GPT_L1 page table to resolve the matching GPA_L1, and issues a KVM_HC_JANUS_OPS hypercall carrying both addresses to L0's #HC Handler (step 2). L0 looks up the host physical address for GPA_L1 and fixes EPT0→2 for GPA_L2 (step 3), then execution resumes at L1 (step 4) and finally back at L2 via VM entry (step 5), where L2's own #PF Handler can proceed. The three privilege bands (L2/v_ring, L1 ring0, L0 ring0) are drawn as stacked boxes with peach-filled handler boxes and a numbered down-and-up arrow path.
summary_zh: 图9展示JANUS的EPT缺页处理:L2访问未映射GPA_L2触发#VE直达L1(步骤1);L1查表得GPA_L1并向L0发hypercall(步骤2);L0修复EPT0→2(步骤3);再依次恢复L1(4)与L2(5),仅需两次退出。
